thread:
rachel.p: Hey team  strange one. My partner and I welcomed our baby via international surrogacy last week. The hospital issued a local birth certificate but US passport/SSN processing will take months. Can we add the baby to Redwood benefits now or do we need the SSN first?

maria.peopleops: Congrats Rachel! Surrogacy births are handled case-by-case but yes, you can start a QLE for a newborn. Carriers often accept provisional docs (foreign/local birth cert + parentage/legal documentation) while SSN is pending. Important: we need the legal parentage paperwork that shows you and your partner are the legal parents (court order or adoption/parentage decree).

rachel.p: We have the hospital birth cert and the court-issued parentage order from the country where the surrogacy occurred. It's in the local language. Will that suffice?

julian.legal: Quick legal note: for international surrogacy, carriers typically require an English translation of foreign documents plus either an apostille or notarized translation depending on the country. Also, US consular birth registration or a certified copy of the foreign parentage order is helpful. If possible, get an apostille and certified translation to reduce back-and-forth.

maria.peopleops: Docs checklist we usually send to carriers for surrogacy/international births:
- Foreign/local birth certificate (PDF) + certified English translation if not English
- Court parentage/decree establishing you as legal parents (PDF) + translation/apostille if available
- US consular report of birth abroad (if obtained) or proof of passport application in process
- If SSN pending, a carrier-friendly letter from the court or consulate stating parentage/passport appl can help
Upload to People Ops portal > Benefits > QLE uploads or email benefits@redwood.com with subject: "QLE: Add newborn - surrogacy - <Rachel P>".

benefits-bot: Received any uploads? If you attach, we'll create a case and assign an ID, then start carrier submission. Typical carrier verification for international docs: 5-12 business days.

rachel.p: We uploaded the court order and the translated birth cert just now. No SSN yet; passport app is filed but pending.

benefits-bot: Upload received. Case #RB-2407 created. We'll submit to medical, dental, and vision carriers. Expect 5-12 business days for verification; carriers may ask for apostille or consular paperwork.

kevin.payroll: Payroll chime  if carrier accepts coverage effective date as the birth date, we can prorate premiums from that date. If carrier sets effective date when SSN is added, deductions might start later and could be retroactive. We will estimate deduction adjustments after carrier confirms effective date. If you need an urgent predetermination for an appointment, let us know provider/date.

rachel.p: We're worried about an appointment next week (well-baby check). If coverage isn't confirmed by then, what do we do?

eve.broker: For urgent visits we can request a predetermination/coverage letter from the medical carrier using provisional docs. That often suffices for the provider to bill as in-network. If the provider insists on SSN, they can still file when the SSN is issued and submit claims retroactively. Send me the provider name and appt date and I'll start the predetermination.

julian.legal: Also, if there are delays with apostille, a notarized translation + consulate letter showing passport application in process tends to placate carriers in many cases. We can draft a short cover letter tying the parentage order to the carrier submission if helpful.

rachel.p: Thanks Julian. I'll DM the appt info to Eve and upload the consulate passport receipt. Any chance Redwood can expedite payroll if carrier confirms early?

kevin.payroll: If carrier confirms a retro effective date before payroll lock for the pay period, we can prorate in the usual cycle. If confirmation comes after payroll locks, we'll process an adjustment on the next cycle. If you flag the case as time-sensitive we can prioritize.

maria.peopleops: Sounds good. Rachel, once you DM Eve the appt and upload the passport receipt we'll push the carrier and request predetermination. We'll update this thread when we have carrier responses and the estimated payroll impact. Welcome to parenthood and congrats again! :heart:
